The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $tan⁡\theta .$
sources.solution:
![](images/21/21170c11aa5ff0ab39b86f94588e5e8a0fa178d0c34b9aa1774ee9f07a4d0812.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=cos⁡\theta ,\,y=sin⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
sin⁡\theta =\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{45}{49}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{4}{49}} \\  & =\pm \frac{2}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =\frac{2}{7}.$

Finally, knowing that $tan⁡\theta =\frac{sin⁡\theta }{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
tan⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{7})}{(\frac{2}{7})}=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{2}.
$$

![](images/e2/e2323a87ec4ab790714f4f6f5e5ff359495e93c6be5d76ae4b9f7ff15d14fd90.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=cos⁡\theta ,\,y=sin⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{\sqrt{14}}{5}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
sin⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{14}}{5}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{14}}{5}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{\sqrt{14}}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{14}{25}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{11}{25}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{11}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{11}}{5}.$

Knowing that $tan⁡\theta =\frac{sin⁡\theta }{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
tan⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{14}}{5})}{(\frac{\sqrt{11}}{5})}=\frac{\sqrt{14}}{\sqrt{11}}.
$$

Finally, we rationalize the denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}tan⁡\theta  & =\frac{\sqrt{14}}{\sqrt{11}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{14}}{\sqrt{11}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{11}}{\sqrt{11}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{14\cdot 11}}{11} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{154}}{11}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Substituting $cos⁡\theta =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{12}{25}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{13}{25}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{13}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $sin⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. Therefore $sin⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{13}}{5}.$

Knowing that $tan⁡\theta =\frac{sin⁡\theta }{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}tan⁡\theta  & =\frac{\sqrt{13}}{2\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{13}}{2\sqrt{3}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{13\cdot 3}}{2\cdot 3} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{39}}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{1}{8},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta .$
sources.solution:
Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{1}{8}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{8}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{8}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{1}{8})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{1}{64}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{63}{64}} \\  & =\pm \frac{3\sqrt{7}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{3\sqrt{7}}{8}.$

Finally, knowing that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{3\sqrt{7}}{8})}{(\frac{1}{8})}=3\sqrt{7}.
$$
